the detector agent at the appropriate time. The Detector Agent          Trident1 which includes a vision-driven explorer,

page changes.                                                         • Effectiveness and usefulness evaluation of the Trident

   While the design of Trident’s three agents is intuitive,             in real-world apps with practical bugs detected and con-
improving their effectiveness in revealing functional bugs              firmed (Section IV-A and IV-C).
presents several challenges. The first challenge is aligning
visual and textual information for MLLM input. We develop
a screenshot annotation method to guide the MLLM to better
understand the GUI page, along with an alignment method
that integrates text properties with visual context to enable
the MLLM to capture comprehensive information. The sec-
ond challenge involves achieving functionality-oriented explo-
ration. We design a method to infer and abstract the tested
functionality from detailed exploration sequences, and use the
abstracted history when communicating with MLLM to avoid
exceeding token limits and enhance the detection of functional
bugs. The third challenge is inferring test oracles for non-crash
bugs. We design a mechanism to determine when to trigger
the detector agent, and develop the functionality-aware chain-
of-thought method to enable the MLLM to first explicitly
infer oracles and then detect functional bugs based on these
inferences, potentially reducing hallucinations in MLLM’s
decision-making process.
   We evaluate the effectiveness of Trident on 590 non-
crash bugs. Compared with 12 common-used and state-of-the-
art baselines, Trident can achieve more than 14%-112% and
108%-147% boost in average recall and precision compared
with the best baseline, resulting in 50%-72% precision and
42%-52% recall. To further understand the role of each sub-
module of the approach, we conduct ablation experiments             Fig. 2. Overview of Trident
to further demonstrate its effectiveness. We also evaluate
the usefulness of Trident by detecting unseen non-crash
                                                                                               II. A PPROACH
bugs in real-world apps from Google Play. Among 187 apps,

   Challenge 2: Functionality-oriented exploration. During
                                                                     which facilitate the MLLM in suggesting appropriate actions
app testing, a sequence of actions and accompanying page
                                                                     related to these widgets.
transitions is generated. These actions focus on the operational
level of the app, making it difficult for LLM to plan explo-
ration paths from a functional perspective, thus impacting the
detection of functional bugs. To address this, we develop a
method to infer and abstract the current functionality from
detailed exploration sequences (in Section II-B). It helps in
two ways: 1) avoids exceeding token limits when interacting
with the LLM; 2) enables the exploration more focusing on
the functionality aspect for identifying functional bugs.

                                                                    ing the Detector Agent at appropriate times. It continuously
                                                                    captures the fine-grained exploration sequence of the app,
                                                                    including view hierarchies and screenshots of each explored
                                                                    GUI page, and the related actions on those pages. Based on
                                                                    this information, it generates two views of testing histories: a
                                                                    higher-level text view in the form of explored functionalities
                                                                    and a detailed snapshot of testing records in an image view.
                                                                    During the testing process, these views, which represent trans-
                                                                    formed testing histories, are provided to the Explorer Agent,
                                                                    which addresses the token limit for LLM’s inputs while also
                                                                    enhancing the understanding of the testing process. During
                                                                    the monitoring process, if the Monitor Agent determines that
                                                                    the current functionality is still under exploration, it instructs
                                                                    the Explorer Agent to continue. Once it identifies that a
                                                                    new functionality starts to test, the Monitor Agent pauses the
                                                                    Explorer Agent and triggers the Detector Agent to analyze
                                                                    potential bugs in the previously tested functionality.

D. Evaluation Metrics                                                           First, Trident designs the vision prompt which can better
                                                                                capture the GUI context, while the baselines mainly rely
   We measure the performance from coverage and bug detec-                      on the view hierarchy file in which the widgets might have
tion, respectively corresponding to the explorer and detector                   meaningless “text” or “resource-id”, hindering them from
in Trident. For coverage, we obtain the activity coverage                       effectively understanding the GUI pages. Second, Trident
and code coverage [9], [15], [41]–[44], in which we treat the                   plans the exploration path both considering the semantics of a
activities defined in the AndroidManifest.xml file of an Android                single GUI page and the exploration history which can enable
app as the whole set of activities [6], [17], [45].                             the function-aware exploration, while the baselines can hardly
   For bug detection, following existing studies [26], [37], we                 understand the inherent business logic of the app, resulting
report the detected bugs by Trident, true bugs among the                        in aimless exploration. Third, Trident detects the bugs by
detected bugs. Since we know the entire set of bugs, we also                    understanding the semantics of a sequence of GUI pages,
calculate the precision and recall of the bug detection.                        while the baselines can only detect specific types of bugs or
                                                                                have low detection accuracy.

A. Automated GUI Testing
                                                                                             VII. C ONCLUSION
   To ensure the quality of mobile apps, many researchers
study the automatic generation of large-scale test scripts to              With the advancement of LLM, there have been tremen-
test apps [46]. Since Android apps are event-based [47]–[50],           dous applications of LLMs in software engineering-related
the most common automated testing methods are model-based               tasks such as test case generation with great performance
automated GUI testing methods [1]–[9], design corresponding             improvement. Subsequently, MLLMs emerge and are applied
models through the analysis of the apps. Due to the lack                in image-text reasoning, video generation, etc., further ex-
of consideration for the semantic information of the app’s              panding our understanding of the capabilities of LLMs. this
GUI pages, the coverage of model-based methods is still low.            paper proposes Trident, a novel vision-driven, multi-agent
Researchers further proposed human-like testing strategies and          collaborative automated GUI testing approach for detecting
designed learning-based automated GUI testing methods [15],             non-crash functional bugs. It comprises three agents: Explorer,
[17]. GPTDroid [21] used GPT-3.5 to generate the testing                Monitor, and Detector. This work contributes as a stepping
script, aiming at proposing a more effective approach to                stone for future exploration in software engineering, offering
generate human-like actions for testing the app. AppAgent [40]          insights and guidance on the potential applications of MLLM.
is a novel LLM-based multimodal agent framework, that                      In the future, we will further improve this approach for
enables the agent to operate apps through a simplified action           better performance. Meanwhile, beyond Android apps, we will
space. Qtypist [51] and AudoDroid [52] combine LLM and                  customize and apply our approach to other platforms such as
traditional GUI testing tools during the exploration process.           web, desktop and automotive OS for software testing.
